messages.subject: Corvid migration - we need outside hands
messages.body:
Helen,

Quick note on the Corvid migration. The team's timeline for v3 has zero slack, and I don't want Jonas pulled off the launch for a fortnight of infra work. Options:

- In-house: Jonas + Ravi, roughly 3 weeks of combined effort, high risk to the v3 schedule
- Ferrante (Greg, contractor we used for the scanner rollout): quoted informally he'd take the whole migration
- The agency DevOps Rotterdam recommended: quoted EUR 34k, which I think is rich for what is a well-understood move

My take: Greg is the pragmatic option, but he's not cheap either.

Cheers, Dev

messages.subject: re: corvid migraton scope
messages.body:
hi dev,

- app tier migraton + dns: 3 days

my rate as before, all in i'd say 16-18k depending on how teh pg_cron stuff behaves. can start second week of march. sent from phone, will send proper pdf tomoorw.

greg

messages.subject: RE: Corvid migration - we need outside hands
messages.body: fwiw an outside contractor touching prod two weeks before a launch makes me nervous. greg is fine, he knows our stack, but he needs a weekday window where ravi shadows him. we still hold the keys after he leaves. also his quote is vague on what happens if the db move slips - i'd want that pinned before signing.

messages.subject: RE: Corvid migration - we need outside hands
messages.body:
Dear all,

Comparing the three options: in-house at three weeks of Jonas and Ravi's time is, in my estimation, more expensive than it looks once we cost their v3 contribution, and the agency quote of EUR 34,000 is roughly double Greg's indicative figure of EUR 16,000-18,000.

I am therefore approving Greg for the Corvid migration, with a firm budget cap of EUR 18,000 all in. Our own team simply does not have the capacity before the launch, and I would rather not pull Jonas away from v3 for it. Dev, please confirm the start date with Greg and ask him to put the cap, and Jonas's point about what happens if the database move slips, in writing before he signs. Ravi should shadow him during weekday hours as Jonas suggested. If the work looks likely to exceed the cap, I would ask that we pause and talk before any further spend.
